citation: MIP-9, section 3 (docs/mip/0009-group-conversation.md): the message box opens addressed to whoever last wrote to the human when that author can be addressed, otherwise to nobody; Reply changes the recipients; a message starting with @ and a member's name addresses that member, several at the start address several, Backspace straight after one turns it back into text, and an @ later only completes. That a later leading name adds to recipients a leading name set, and that a name the human turned back into text is not taken again, are the implementation's own reading.
why: The message box decides whom the human's words reach. A draft opened to Muster, a name typed mid-sentence that silently readdressed the post, or a recipient the human removed coming back each sends a message somewhere the human did not mean.

cases.name: it opens addressed to the last member who wrote to the human
cases.why: The likeliest thing the human does on opening a conversation is answer the question that brought them there.

cases.name: it opens addressed to nobody when the last author to the human is Muster
cases.why: @muster is never an addressee; and falling back to an older author would address somebody the human was not answering.

cases.name: it opens addressed to nobody when the last author to the human left
cases.why: A post to an author who left is refused, so opening addressed to them leads the human into a refusal.

cases.name: a leading @ and a member's name addresses that member instead
cases.why: Typing @heron and a space is the quick way to address somebody else; it replaces the recipient the draft opened with rather than adding to it.

cases.name: several names at the start address several
cases.why: MIP-9: several at the start address several, so the second name joins the first rather than replacing it.

cases.name: a callsign addresses the pane participant it names
cases.why: The human types the name they see, otter, and the post must address the participant, whose name is its pane id.

cases.name: an @ later in the text completes the name and stays text
cases.why: Only a leading @ addresses: mentioning somebody mid-sentence must not readdress the post.

cases.name: a leading name that is not a member stays text
cases.why: Readdressing a post to a name nobody in the group answers to would be refused; the human may also just be starting a sentence with an @.

cases.name: Backspace straight after a recipient turns it back into text
cases.why: A recipient taken by mistake has to be undoable with the key the human reaches for, and the name must come back as they typed it.

cases.name: a name turned back into text is not taken again by the next keystroke
cases.why: Otherwise the name the human just released would snap back into a recipient as soon as they typed anything else.

cases.name: Reply addresses the author, and a leading name then replaces it
cases.why: Reply is the human choosing a recipient; a name typed at the start after it is a change of mind, not an addition.

cases.name: a completion at the start of the text addresses the member
cases.why: Choosing a name from the list is typing it, so at the start it takes the member as a recipient as typing `@otter ` would.

cases.name: a completion later in the text completes the name and stays text
cases.why: Only a leading @ addresses; a name later in a message is part of what it says.

cases.name: a completion to somebody who is not a member completes nothing
cases.why: A list that went stale while the human chose from it must not write a name the post would be refused for.

cases.name: completion offers members, never Muster or the human
cases.why: Neither can be addressed by the human's post, so offering them only leads to a refusal.

cases.name: Urgent is kept with the draft
cases.why: A draft is kept whole; dropping Urgent would send an urgent answer as an ordinary one.

cases.name: picking a question's answer addresses its author, and the post is the answer and the note
cases.why: Picking fills the message box rather than sending it, so a note can go with it (MIP-9, section 6), and an answer goes to whoever asked, as Reply addresses them. The post's body starts with the answer, as every reply that picks one does.

cases.name: a picked answer is kept through typing, and picking it again takes it back
cases.why: The draft is kept whole, the pick with it, so writing the note does not lose the answer; and the banner's rule holds here too, so one gesture undoes a pick.

cases.name: picking the picked answer again takes it back
cases.why: As in the banner: one gesture picks, and the same gesture undoes it.

cases.name: a question asked of another agent takes no pick
cases.why: The daemon refuses an answer from somebody a question was not asked of, so the pick would end in a refusal after the human had written their note.

expect.refused: #1 is not a question asked of you in this conversation, so nothing was picked

cases.name: a question answered by somebody else takes no pick
cases.why: A question takes one answer; the human would only be refused by the daemon after writing a note.

expect.refused: #2 was answered already, by heron: Yes; nothing was picked

cases.name: a pick names one of the question's own answers
cases.why: The answer is sent by its words, so a number past the last names nothing the question offered.

expect.refused: #1 offers 2 answers, so answer 3 is none of them; nothing was picked
